name: Karnātaka
summary_text: This division was covered by the dedicated country dossier: the country-level research identified no Karnataka-specific enforcement series or incident pattern material enough to score separately (±0.02), so it is assessed at the national score. Karnataka is, however, one of only 12 states/UTs that have constituted the legally mandated transgender welfare board — an official-willingness marker the dossier notes on the RTI finding that most such boards remain largely leaderless.

sources.title: India’s Transgender Rights Bill a Huge Setback | Human Rights Watch
sources.claim_summary: Human Rights Watch statement (26 March 2026) on India's 2026 Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Amendment Bill, passed by parliament: removes self-identification, limits legal recognition to hijra and kinner communities and intersex people, mandates medical certification, and adds offences with up to life imprisonment for "coercing or alluring" someone to be transgender. National law applying uniformly in Karnataka; the piece carries no Karnataka-specific findings.

sources.title: Transgender Bill: India parliament passes amendment to redefine transgender identity amid protests
sources.claim_summary: BBC report (26 March 2026): both houses passed the amendment removing self-identification, restricting recognition to biological/physical traits, intersex variations and traditional identities, with mandatory medical-board certification for gender-affirming surgery; community and opposition protests, a Supreme Court-appointed panel sought withdrawal, presidential assent pending. Applies nationally including Karnataka; no regional coverage in the piece.

Times of India (Kolkata edition, 18 August 2024): a transwoman alleged an RPF constable groped her for a "gender check" at Rabindra Sadan metro station en route to an RG Kar protest; authorities denied it and filed a counter-FIR. A West Bengal incident, not about Karnataka, held as a national datapoint on screening conduct toward gender-nonconforming people in public transit spaces.
